sentences.text: The animal possessed a skull that was proportionally large, long, and pointed, featuring oval-shaped eye sockets, antorbital openings, and temporal openings.
Its body was covered by small overlapping osteoderms, or bony scutes, which protected many of its vertebrae.
The scapula of Diandongosuchus is longer and narrower than the scapula of the related species Qianosuchus.
The type species Diandongosuchus fuyuanensis was named in 2012 from fossils found in the Zhuganpo Formation of Yunnan Province.
Fossil evidence suggests Diandongosuchus ate small vertebrates like fish, indicated by bones found near the hips likely representing stomach contents.
Skull characteristics shared with phytosaurs in Diandongosuchus, such as jaw joint shapes, likely strengthened the skull and bite for hunting.
Researchers suggest Diandongosuchus may have had a lifestyle similar to modern saltwater crocodiles, living along coastlines without being fully marine.
The animal belongs to the class Reptilia.
Later studies by Stocker et al. (2016, 2017) reclassified Diandongosuchus as the basalmost known phytosaur.
Diandongosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic period in China.
Diandongosuchus fossils were found in a Ladinian-age marine limestone formation.
The species lived during the Ladinian stage, between 241.464 and 237 million years ago.
